newsitem.title: USA: FAA urges parents to keep children buckled up.
newsitem.headline: FAA urges parents to keep children buckled up.

text.p: With the Christmas travel season approaching, federal aviation officials urged parents Tuesday to make sure their children are buckled up when flying to protect against turbulence injuries.

"Aviation continues to be the safest way to travel, but passengers need to be aware that unpredicted turbulence does happen," said Linda Hall Daschle, acting administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration.
She told a news conference that each year about 60 people not wearing a seat belt while the "fasten seat belt" sign was on were injured by turbulence, making it the biggest cause of in-flight injury.
Daschle advised passengers to wear seat belts at all times to protect against unexpected turbulence caused by phenomena such as jet streams, cold and warm fronts and thunderstorms.
She said children younger than 2 were not required to have seats and were at risk from turbulence when on a parent's lap.
Daschle urged parents to get seats for children and to use chlld car safety devices on their airplane seats.
She said parents not buying seats for children should try to fly at off-peak times when airlines were more likely to have empty seats. The parent must provide the restraint devices, she added.
She urged airlines to try to make fares for children more affordable. She said Southwest Airlines was a leader in offering low-price family fares.
